title: A single Operational Facilitator decides within seven days whether a Grove proposal is allowed to reach a vote
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.3 gives the Operational Facilitator seven days to "review the Root Edit Proposal for alignment," then splits the outcome. If aligned, they announce the finding on the Forum post and "must also confirm that the proposal is feasible for Operational GovOps to operationalize." If misaligned, they "announce their finding and provide the reasoning for it." They must additionally "determine whether the proposal results in an increase in the on-chain risk to the protocol" and state that determination publicly.

This single role therefore performs three distinct functions in one act: **constitutional review** (does this violate the Atlas or the Grove Artifact), **operational triage** (can GovOps actually execute it), and **risk classification** (does this trigger the Core Council Risk Advisor gate). Bundling them is efficient but concentrates a great deal of discretion.

A.6.1.1.2.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.4 makes the gate binding: the Facilitator triggers the Snapshot poll only "where their review of the proposal results in a finding of alignment." A misalignment finding is therefore terminal for that proposal cycle — the section specifies no appeal, no override vote, and no route for token holders to overrule the finding.

The safeguard the Atlas relies on instead is **forced public reasoning**: the Facilitator must publish why. Accountability is reputational and after-the-fact rather than procedural.
description: The review bundles three judgments — alignment, operational feasibility, and whether on-chain risk increases — and a misalignment finding stops the proposal before any token holder votes.
